chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man comes to me with silver coins (wariq) to sell them, intending to get silver from me; I am certain that he does not want gold dinars, he wants only silver, and he does not leave until he takes my silver, so I buy dirhams from him with dinars, so his dinars are not complete in my possession, so I borrow for him from my neighbor, and give him the full amount of his dinars, and perhaps I do not secure their weight. He said: 'Does he not take the fulfillment of what is due to him?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell silver for gold if the buyer pays in installments or incomplete amounts?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates a currency exchange (bay' al-darham bi al-dinar) where the seller accepts gold in lieu of silver, even if the gold is not immediately weighed or fully secured, provided the creditor receives the full value owed (wafa'). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that in spot currency transactions, the primary condition is the fulfillment of the debt's value rather than the immediate physical possession or perfect weighing of the specific coins, distinguishing it from riba al-fadl concerns.
